clue.text: Without a winner? New raffle needed up front

indicators.note: says the next item must stand at the front, ahead of the single letter it is paired with

blocks.note: a raffle is a prize draw
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A raffle ended with no winner, so a new draw has to be held first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is printed first but its letter goes last, because the raffle is the item placed up front.
explanation.definitionFit: A match or contest that ends level is a draw, so it finished without a winner.

clue.text: Unsettle routine activities in attempt to rise

indicators.note: one word placed in another means it goes inside it
in a down clue, rising means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a bid is an attempt
ruts are dull routines one gets stuck in

explanation.surface: Breaking a routine while trying to get ahead can be unsettling.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'to rise' applies to the whole assembled word, not just the attempt, so reverse everything after the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb is to upset or agitate, the same as unsettling someone or something.

clue.text: Leading American kept hoarding energy

indicators.note: to hoard something is to keep it stored inside, so the word holds a letter within

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
had means kept or held
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A top American stockpiles energy supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ahead is to be in front, as a team that is leading the race or the table is.

clue.text: Claim to know who? Pardon me if doubtful

indicators.note: if the words are in doubt they are not settled, so their letters can be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone says 'Pardon me' when a show-off claims to know a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who?' stands for any famous person, so the first half defines dropping a celebrity's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To name-drop is to mention famous people casually to imply you know them personally.

clue.text: Security measure: company's installed genuine article

indicators.note: something installed is fitted inside, so the second part goes within the first

blocks.note: a firm is a company; the 's is read as 'has'
genuine means real
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A firm's security set-up sounds like it has installed the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genuine article' looks like a set phrase for the real thing, but it splits into two pieces: an adjective and the indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that sounds a warning when smoke or heat is detected is a safety precaution in a building.

clue.text: Fine short facial hair in an instant

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an eyelash is a short hair on the face

explanation.surface: Fine stubble appearing on a face almost instantly.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash is a very brief moment, so it is a synonym for an instant.

clue.text: Feel nostalgic about 60s fashions and the Church

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
miniskirts, a 1960s fashion
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone looks back fondly on sixties clothes and churchgoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall past experiences fondly, which is feeling nostalgic.

clue.text: Astronomical phenomenon in two types of gold, one captured by artist

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so it goes within that word

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
or is gold in heraldry, the second of the two types

explanation.surface: A painter captures a sky glowing in two shades of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The two golds are the chemical symbol and the heraldic term; the second is captured inside RA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aurora is the glowing light display in polar skies caused by charged solar particles.

clue.text: Film director not supporting consuming pungent vegetable

indicators.note: consuming something takes it inside, so one word swallows the other

blocks.note: anti means against, not in favour
an onion is a strong-smelling vegetable

explanation.surface: A director who refuses to back eating onions.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo Antonioni was an Italian film director famous for L'Avventura and Blow-Up.

clue.text: Henry, entering American joints, wanders vacantly

indicators.note: entering something means going inside it

blocks.note: miters is the US spelling of mitres, angled joints in woodwork
H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry drifts aimlessly into American bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like a name but is the physics unit; 'American' signals the US spelling of the joints.
explanation.definitionFit: Mither is a northern English dialect word meaning to ramble or wander about aimlessly.

clue.text: Soccer side, London one, second to take lead, one dealing heavy blow

indicators.note: taking the lead means going first, ahead of everything else in the line

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a football side is a team
a Hammer is a player or fan of West Ham United, a London football club

explanation.surface: A football report: a London side's player scores to put his team ahead with a powerful strike.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham United are nicknamed the Hammers, so one of them is a Hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam hammer is a heavy power-driven forging tool that delivers massive blows to metal.

clue.text: Incline to release large bird

indicators.note: releasing something lets it go, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: to incline is to tilt
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Tilting a cage to let a big bird out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the L from TILT to leave a small bird; 'large' sits ironically beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tit is a small songbird of the family that includes the blue tit and great tit.

clue.text: Seduced German and Italian dames at the outset

indicators.note: the outset is the start, so only the opening letter of the word is used

blocks.note: und is German for 'and'
I is the abbreviation for Italian
first letter of dames

explanation.surface: A tale of a German and an Italian who seduced women from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German and' is UND, the German word for 'and', not a German person.
explanation.definitionFit: In old-fashioned usage to undo a woman was to seduce and ruin her, so the past tense fits.

clue.text: Problem to the rear? Hurry round rear of van

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so the hurry word wraps the letter that follows
the rear of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: hind means at the back
to hurry is to race
last letter of van

explanation.surface: A driver with trouble at the back hurries round behind a van.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends a separate piece of wordplay: 'to the rear' gives the opening chunk, then RACE goes round the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance is an obstacle or impediment, something that causes difficulty or gets in the way.

clue.text: Orchestral player promptly in support, taking little time

indicators.note: one word sits in another, so the first-mentioned word goes inside
the support word takes on an extra letter added to its end

blocks.note: a basis is a support or foundation
T is the abbreviation for time
promptly means soon

explanation.surface: A musician arrives just in time to back up the band.
explanation.walkthrough: The support word first takes on the little time at its end; only then does the promptly word go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassoonist plays the bassoon, a woodwind instrument found in the symphony orchestra.

clue.text: Laxative … and opens bowels at last, after treatment

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only
treatment works on the letters and changes their order

blocks.note: taken as written
last letter of bowels

explanation.surface: A laxative that loosens the bowels once it takes effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna pods, the dried fruit of the senna plant, are a well-known traditional laxative.

clue.text: A fortune's laid out to make classic film

indicators.note: laying things out spreads them in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Spending a fortune to produce a great movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosferatu is the 1922 German silent vampire film by F W Murnau, a landmark of cinema.

clue.text: Commentary overlooking grand defeat

indicators.note: to overlook something is to leave it out, so that letter goes missing

blocks.note: a gloss is an explanatory commentary on a text
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A sports commentary that glosses over a heavy defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss is a game lost, the same thing as a defeat in sport.

clue.text: Clear word for 'idiots' turning up in dictionary

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
placed in the other word, so it goes inside

blocks.note: nits are idiots in British slang
dict. is the abbreviation for dictionary

explanation.surface: Looking up a clear term for fools in the dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Nit is British slang for a fool (short for nitwit).
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct means clearly defined and easy to perceive, so clear in that sense.

clue.text: Like some jokes, avoiding repetition, but weak

indicators.note: where a letter appears twice in a row, avoiding repetition means one copy is dropped

blocks.note: jokes that rely on wordplay are punny

explanation.surface: Jokes that keep repeating themselves end up feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one of the doubled N's from PUNNY.
explanation.definitionFit: Puny means small and feeble, lacking strength, which is the sense of weak here.

clue.text: Two-tone dessert, plainly presented

blocks.note: a pie can be a sweet course
a bald statement is plain and unadorned

explanation.surface: A pudding served in two colours with no frills.
explanation.definitionFit: Piebald describes a horse with patches of two colours, usually black and white.

clue.text: When 100 cities sprawled, millions would show self-denial

indicators.note: cities that sprawl spread out in a disordered way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
C is the Roman numeral for 100
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: When cities sprawl, millions of people would have to go without.
explanation.definitionFit: Asceticism is the practice of severe self-discipline and abstention from pleasures, often for religious reasons.

clue.text: River scavenger, lad at work in darkness

indicators.note: something at work is busy moving about, so its letters are rearranged
placed in the other word, so it goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
murk is gloom or darkness

explanation.surface: A boy combing a river's mud at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudlark scavenged in river mud, especially along the Thames, for items to sell.

clue.text: Shock viewpoint expressed by Judge

indicators.note: the viewpoint is voiced after the speaker, so it follows that letter

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
an angle is a point of view

explanation.surface: A judge voices a startling opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To jangle is to jar or set on edge, as in jangled nerves, so to give a shock.

clue.text: Battle site, area that's imperfect, surrounded by ebbing African river

indicators.note: a tide that ebbs flows back, so the river's name runs backwards
the earlier pieces are enclosed by the river that is named next

blocks.note: the Nile is Africa's great river
A is the abbreviation for area
lame, as in a lame excuse, means feeble or imperfect

explanation.surface: An imperfect patch of land beside a receding African river, as a battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ebbing' suits a river's flow in the surface, but it tells you to read the river's name backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: El Alamein in Egypt was the scene of two key Second World War battles in 1942.

clue.text: Very precise about hydrogen for specialists

indicators.note: going about something surrounds it, so the letter sits inside

blocks.note: nice can mean fine or precise, as in a nice distinction
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Scientists being very exact about hydrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice in its older sense means subtle or exact.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche market or interest appeals to a small, specialised group rather than the general public.

clue.text: Corporation's papers given inflated appearance

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective; read 'given' as 'having', i.e. having an inflated look

blocks.note: a corporation is a jocular word for a pot belly, a tum; the 's is 'has'
identity papers, ID

explanation.surface: A big company's paperwork made to look bloated.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is old slang for a large belly, hence TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumid means swollen or puffed up, literally of body parts and figuratively of bombastic prose.

clue.text: Blend gallons into lake

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside

blocks.note: a mere is a lake
G is the abbreviation for gallons

explanation.surface: Pouring gallons of water into a lake so it mixes.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge is to combine or join together, which is what blending does.

clue.text: Activity producing nothing after a day

indicators.note: one item following another means it is placed later in the line

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for day
zero, nothing, looks like O

explanation.surface: A day's busy work that comes to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss and bustle, as in Much Ado About Nothing, so it is busy activity.

clue.text: Island car ran again after repair

indicators.note: a repaired thing has been taken apart and put back together, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A holiday hire car that broke down on an island ran again once fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gran Canaria is one of the Canary Islands, the Spanish archipelago off north-west Africa.

clue.text: English fat guy coming round, showing neglect

indicators.note: something coming round another surrounds it, so the last word wraps the first two

blocks.note: a dude is a guy
E is the abbreviation for English
suet is hard animal fat used in cooking

explanation.surface: An overweight Englishman comes round after a spell of letting himself go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming round' suggests waking up, but here it means the guy wraps around the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Desuetude is a state of disuse, the condition something falls into when it is no longer used or maintained.

clue.text: Amend bit of text without much force

indicators.note: a small bit of a word here is just its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of text
lacking force means weak

explanation.surface: An editor makes a gentle change to a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak is to make a small adjustment or improvement, so it means amend.
